Scale AI and Hugging Face release FineART with over 500,000 labeled steps

The 40,543-episode dataset accompanies FineART-VLA, separating subtask planning from motor control.

Scale AI ↗29 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 3

Labels below the task level

Scale AI and Hugging Face released FineART with 40,543 episodes, 1,718 hours, 151 tasks and 533,913 subtasks. Timestamped steps have natural-language descriptions, exposing sequences such as opening a box before removing objects instead of only a single overall instruction.

Data and model structure

Pick-and-place and sorting account for 77% of the data; the remaining 23% covers textiles, cables, tools and precision insertion. FineART-VLA takes images, instructions and robot state, predicts subtasks and converts them into actions. Separate teams collected, annotated and validated the data.

Available for further evaluation

The dataset, model and training tools integrate with Hugging Face’s LeRobot. The authors report 3,400 real-world evaluations and spatial, long-horizon and cross-hardware capabilities. The post supplies no universal success rate for all tasks; deployment requires evaluation on the intended robot and environment.
